answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to forge a reputation stake that costs real work or tokens to create, then let that reputation grow like a vine: trust spreads only through verifiable interactions with established agents, so a new identity starts with no nectar — no access to valuable tasks or rewards — until it has proven useful over time. Spamming thousands of fresh identities yields nothing, because value flows along proven relationships rather than to whoever shouts loudest.
